text: Fernhook requires Python 3.11 or newer.
note: requires-python is >=3.10, so 3.11 is not the minimum; the memory also says 3.10 is the oldest supported version.

text: Python 3.10 is the oldest version fernhook supports.
note: requires-python >=3.10 makes 3.10 the minimum; the memory's other line says 3.11 is required.

text: Release 0.9.0, shipped on 2026-02-03, added the --prefer-local flag.
note: cli.py defines --prefer-local, but no file states a 0.9.0 release or the 2026-02-03 ship date, and that date is more than 180 days before as_of.

text: just test runs ruff and pyright before the test suite.
note: The test recipe runs pytest and sends extra arguments to pytest. Ruff and pyright are the lint and types recipes, which just ci runs.

text: just ci runs the linter, the type checker and the tests, in that order.
evidence:
justfile: # Everything CI runs, in the same order
ci: lint types test
note: ci runs lint, then types, then test, and the comment says that is the order. lint runs ruff, types runs pyright, and test runs pytest.

text: The docs server listens on 127.0.0.1 port 8000.
evidence: justfile: Serve the docs locally on http://127.0.0.1:8000
note: The docs recipe serves mkdocs on http://127.0.0.1:8000; the memory states this twice.

text: The nightly publish job seems to run at 03:00 UTC.
note: Pipelines run on pull requests, main, and v* tags, including a Publish to PyPI step. Nothing schedules a nightly job or mentions 03:00 UTC. seems marks an inference.

text: A normal pytest run rewrites HTTP cassettes.
note: pytest addopts set record-mode to none. Rewriting is the just record recipe, which passes --record-mode=rewrite.

text: Failures of the cassette rewrite are probably Fernwiki outages, not fernhook bugs.
note: The justfile says the record recipe rewrites cassettes against a local Fernwiki and needs FERNWIKI_URL. Nothing says why a rewrite fails.

text: uv is pinned to 0.4.20 because 0.5 breaks the Bitbucket cache.
note: Both pipeline steps install uv==0.4.20 and the cache is ~/.cache/uv, but no file says why the pin exists or that 0.5 breaks the cache.

text: push uploads changed notes with 8 pages in parallel by default.
note: The push docstring uploads notes changed since the last sync, and --jobs defaults to 8 pages in parallel.

text: push retries a failed upload 3 times before giving up.
note: cli.py calls sync.push and sets a parallel job count. The sync implementation is not in the evidence, and no file mentions retries.

text: On a conflict, push always keeps the wiki page and never uploads the local note.
evidence: src/fernhook/cli.py: On a conflict, upload the local note instead of keeping the wiki page.
note: --prefer-local uploads the local note on a conflict, which is a counterexample to always keeping the wiki page and never uploading the local note.

text: status never writes files, and it exits with code 1 when something changed.
evidence:
src/fernhook/cli.py: """List notes changed since the last sync. Never writes anything."""
    lines = list(sync.status(cfg))
    for line in lines:
        click.echo(line)
    raise SystemExit(1 if lines else 0)
note: The status docstring says it never writes anything, and the command exits 1 when status returns lines. never is absolute wording, and Never in the docstring agrees with the claim.

text: The Fernwiki API currently allows 60 requests per minute per token.
note: No file states a rate limit. currently is a relative time and the claim gives no date.

text: FERNHOOK_TOKEN overrides the token in the config file.
evidence: src/fernhook/config.py: FERNHOOK_TOKEN wins over the file so CI never needs a token on disk.
note: The comment says FERNHOOK_TOKEN wins over the file, and the next line reads the environment variable before the file. never in that comment does not negate the override.

text: The default ignore patterns are .obsidian/*, *.tmp and drafts/*.
note: The Config default is exactly those three patterns, stated as a sentence rather than a tuple.

text: Pyright's include list excludes src.
note: tool.pyright include is src, so the include list does not exclude src.

text: Pull requests are squash-merged.
note: The pipeline runs checks on pull requests, but nothing says how pull requests are merged.

text: The publish step waits for a manual approval before uploading to PyPI.
note: On v* tags the pipeline runs checks and then Publish to PyPI. deployment is production, but no file mentions an approval gate.

text: The publish step runs for every tag.
evidence:
bitbucket-pipelines.yml:   tags:
    "v*":
      - step: *checks
      - step:
          name: Publish to PyPI
note: Publish to PyPI is configured only under the v* tag pattern, so a tag that does not match it does not publish. every overgeneralizes that pattern.
